texts: good. the equinox witness carries its kind, its genus, the rank ('second'), the day, the year and past tense as separate queryable atoms, and treating 'came' as the equinox simply occurring is the right reading here.

bad: a calendar year used as a clause participant has nowhere licensed to go, so the translator dropped the calendar term (Year 2) straight into the subject slot, where only an ordinary entity symbol belongs — the atom is ill-typed and no query will match it. Give the year a kind word so it becomes a proper named thing: "The year named Year 2 began on day 365." Be aware of one residual limit no rewrite fixes: even the correct entity for the year will not be connected to the (Year 2) time stamps that date the other sentences, so "which year began on day 365?" and "what happened in Year 2?" still live in separate corners of the knowledge base.

mixed: the store, the holding event and the figure are all carried, but 'eight weeks of supply' is a quantity-of phrase the instruction set has no encoding for, so the eight weeks land on an unlabelled dimension — a question asking how long the supply lasts has no dimension to ask about. Name the dimension with a verb instead: "The feather store held a supply lasting eight weeks."

bad: 'about ten' cannot be recorded — an exact count must be a plain integer and the vague-count phrases carry no number at all, so the hedged figure was improvised into the count slot and the rule-abiding outcome would be to drop the number entirely. State the hedge as a bound instead: "At least nine and at most eleven sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning." If the approximation is not load-bearing, "Ten sky-cats were visible on the cliff-spires in the morning." parses exactly. Everything else in the sentence is fine — the group, the spires, the morning, and a per-cat visibility rule that does fire.

mixed: the store, its winter supply and the eleven weeks are all carried, but as in the feather-store sentence 'eleven weeks of winter supply' has no licensed encoding, so the figure sits on an unlabelled dimension. Same fix: "The salt-bloom store held a winter supply lasting eleven weeks."

mixed: nothing is lost — the denial, the still-expected recovery ('yet'), the losses and their Year 1 timing all come through — but 'recovered from' is a prepositional verb and its object landed in the spatial 'whence' slot rather than the slot named after the preposition, so a question worded with 'from' will miss it. If that retrieval matters, drop the preposition: "The mire-essence store had not yet recovered the losses of Year 1."
